Class XtensaAsmBackend

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.backend.xtensa.XtensaAsmBackend
All Implemented Interfaces:
AsmBackend
public final class XtensaAsmBackend extends Object implements AsmBackend
Emits GNU Xtensa assembly (the Nano ESP32's ESP32-S3, an LX7 core) straight from Juno IR, with the storage model of Thumb2AsmBackend: every IR value and JVM local lives in a fixed stack slot (see FrameLayout.packed(IrMethod)) and registers are only scratch within one instruction. The C++ runtime shim is the same one Thumb-2 links against (RuntimeShim): its code is plain C++ the ESP32 toolchain compiles as is.

Calling convention

Generated functions follow the windowed-register ABI GCC uses on this core, so C code and generated code call each other directly: a function opens with entry a1, N, reserving its slots at a1+0 upwards plus the 32 bytes of register-window save areas GCC reserves, and returns with retw (the result in a2, or a2/a3). A call passes its first six argument words in a10-a15 through call8 and the rest at a1+0 upwards, the bottom of a frame that then keeps its slots above them.

Scope

This first cut lowers what GPIO, delay and serial programs need: int, long, float and double arithmetic and comparisons, branches and switch, static and instance calls, interface dispatch, lambdas and method references, objects, fields, statics and arrays, plus threads and structured concurrency. Anything else fails with a CompileException rather than generating code that was never checked.

Threads

Juno threads are FreeRTOS tasks of which only one, the holder of a baton, runs Java code (see ThreadRuntime#esp32Port). They are preempted at safepoints, as on AVR: once its time slice is over a thread hands the CPU over on its next loop backedge (juno_thread_backedge) or method entry (juno_thread_safepoint). No register holds a value across those calls, so nothing but the stack needs saving.
